newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures widen opening gains.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures widen opening gains.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures widened opening gains on aggressive dealer buying as the market showed more broad-based leadership, traders and analysts said.
Dealers turned into aggressive buyers after a lackluster opening, with one U.S. firm buying December Standard & Poor 500s through the 747.00 level.
"There were a lot of sell-stops triggered at 747.10, but (the dealer) kept buying through that level," one trader said.
Such activity in the pit soon erased any ideas that S&P futures would succumb to profit-taking on Friday morning.
"If dealers race to buy on the pull-backs then we are not going to see any profit-taking," one trader said.
Dealers disregarded the weak tone in the U.S. bond market and chased December S&Ps to 749.70, just shy of its contract and all-time high of 749.80 set on Wednesday.

Traders said the gains in several technology stocks, besides IBM, lifted the Nasdaq and re-charged the S&P index. For the last several days, cash and futures S&P 500s have lagged behind the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Traders cited the jump in Intel and Microsoft's prices for the firmer tone in the S&P 500 index.
The Nasdaq surged 8.86 points to 1,266.94, outpacing the gains in the Dow Industrials.

Nikkei 225 futures were also higher, but December languished slightly above the 21,000 level. One analyst noted the improvement in Japanese corporate profits may not be enough to shake Japanese investors out of the U.S. bond and stock markets.
Meanwhile, December S&Ps lost the impetus by the end of the first hour of pit trade to re-test 749.70.
"I'm a little disappointed we can't get through there," one trader said.
Fair value for December S&Ps is at 2.10 points to the cash index, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 3.15 and arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 1.05.

At 0944 CST/1544 GMT, December S&P 500s were up 1.75 point to 747.20, KBT value lines were up 2.20 points at 674.70, Nikkeis were up 85.0 at 21,260, Midcap 400s were up 0.80 at 254.50 and Nasdaq 100s were up 9.50 at 814.25.
